correctness.rationale: Coordinate supports give independent false-twin classes of weight \(w_S=\prod_{i\in S}(q_i-1)\), with adjacency exactly disjointness. Any forcing complement uses at most one representative per class. In the mixed case, singleton classes are exactly binary-only supports. A minimal white singleton support is forced from its complementary nonsingleton class; after all singleton whites are removed, a minimal remaining white support is forced from its complement. This proves the complete product polynomial. The Boolean disjointness quotient is unimodular, giving a rank \(2^r-2\) witness; \(M\le Z\) proves equality. Root multiplicities recover binary factors and exact subset-product inversion recovers every nonbinary field order.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves the structurally delicate mixed regime where binary coordinates create singleton support classes but nonbinary coordinates still provide forcing sources. It yields the complete zero forcing polynomial, all minimizers, exact maximum nullity and minimum rank, and reconstructs the finite-field factor orders from root multiplicities. The failure at the pure-binary boundary makes this a natural sharp classification rather than a routine parameter increment.
